question: Whether the inherited annual cash distribution allowance is an observed corporate or legal constraint, and how to expose structural uncertainty without estimating unobserved lawful funds.

sources.finding: Delaware corporation. Cash availability and legally available funds differ. Surplus, profit and solvency conditions are discussed; no automatic annual allowance identified.

Statutory capital and surplus differ from preferred liquidation claims. Dividend and redemption routes have distinct conditions. Board determinations and the net-profits route are not reconstructed here.

Cumulative accrual, declaration, legal availability, cash distribution restrictions, ordinary redemption and open-market repurchase are distinct concepts. No calendar-year dollar allowance identified.

decision: Retain annual allowance as explicitly named institutional stress rule; compare rolling, no-added-allowance, and financial net-asset screens. Do not describe any proxy as actual statutory surplus.
